title: Repo rate reset : Borrowers face higher costs ahead
description: THE Reserve Bank of India has raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, the first increase since February 2023. More significantly, it has shifted its monetary-policy stance from neutral to “calibrated tightening”. The message is clear: containing inflation has once again become a priority. The immediate consequence will be higher borrowing costs. Banks are likely to pass on at least part of the increase to borrowers, pushing up interest rates on floating-rate home, vehicle and personal loans. For households already managing high living costs, higher EMIs could squeeze disposable incomes and moderate consumption. Businesses, too, will face costlier credit, potentially affecting investment decisions.

title: Repo rate reset : Borrowers face higher costs ahead
description: THE Reserve Bank of India has raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, the first increase since February 2023. More significantly, it has shifted its monetary-policy stance from neutral to “calibrated tightening”. The message is clear: containing inflation has once again become a priority. The immediate consequence will be higher borrowing costs. Banks are likely to pass on at least part of the increase to borrowers, pushing up interest rates on floating-rate home, vehicle and personal loans. For households already managing high living costs, higher EMIs could squeeze disposable incomes and moderate consumption. Businesses, too, will face costlier credit, potentially affecting investment decisions.
